question.text:
On D = {(x, y) : x ̸= 0}, let F = (1/x, 0), ϕ = log |x|, and ψ = log |x| + sgn(x). Which statement
is correct?
(A) Only ϕ is a potential.
(B) Only ψ is a potential.
(C) Both are potentials, and their difference is one constant on all of D.
(D) Both are potentials, but their difference has different constants on the two components.
(E) Neither is a potential because D is disconnected.

solution.text:
The sign function is locally constant on D, so its derivatives there are zero. Both gradients
equal (1/x, 0). Their difference is 1 on x > 0 and −1 on x < 0. The usual uniqueness-up-to-
one-constant statement requires a connected domain.

question.text:
2 2 2
For F = (−2x, −2y)/(x + y ) on the punctured plane, what is its integral around any closed
piecewise smooth curve avoiding the origin?
(A) 0
(B) 2π
(C) −2π
(D) 2π times the number of turns around the origin
(E) It is undefined for every curve surrounding the origin.

solution.text:
2 2
The globally defined function ϕ = 1/(x + y ) has gradient F everywhere on this domain.
The endpoint difference is zero for every closed path, even one enclosing the missing point.
A hole permits curl-free fields without potentials, but does not prevent a particular field
from having a potential.
